name: Ned "Nails" Garrity
cause: shot by a night watchman while leaving a house
summary: Housebreaker by trade, some sixty burglaries known. Sole support of a mother and three sisters. Shot in Tanner's Row with nothing on him.

entries.text: Some sixty burglaries over nineteen years.
Beat a receiver of stolen goods who had cheated him.
Informed on his partner to shorten his own sentence.
Kept his mother and three sisters housed and fed, by the only trade he had.
Returned a stolen wedding ring through a letterbox, having read the inscription.

hidden.text: Abandoned the job to carry an old man from a gas-filled house; killed doing it.

archive.title: Watchman's statement; gas report
cards: Watchman Coyle: 'Man come out the FRONT door carrying the old gent. I fired.'
Coldharbour Gas Co.: main burst under 14 Tanner's Row; the house full by 2 a.m.
Householder Abel Penhallow, 81, revived on the step: 'Somebody carried me.'

fact.text: Shot carrying the unconscious householder out of a gas-filled house.

questions.text: Why was there nothing on you?
answer: Bad night. Nothing worth lifting. Write that down and let's get on.
questions.card: Claims it was a bad night with nothing worth lifting.

questions.text: Did you ever hurt anyone in a house?
answer: Never once. You go in quiet, you go out quiet. Out the back. Always out the back.
questions.card: Never hurt anyone in a house. Always left by the back.

questions.text: You went out the front. Carrying him.
answer: Stupidest thing I ever did. Twenty years out the back and the one time I use the front door...
He was just lying there. What was I meant to do, step over him?
questions.card: Calls the rescue the stupidest thing he ever did. Wouldn't step over him.

fact.text: Broke his one rule, the front door, to carry the old man out.

heaven: He is seen at the Gilt Gate checking the hinges out of habit, then, visibly, deciding not to.
hell: The old man from Tanner's Row arrives in the queue eleven days later.
He asks every clerk in the hall where the burglar went.

ext.mitigating: Hides his one great deed because he is ashamed of it as bad workmanship.
